title: Impact of Growth Medium: Baculovirus Replication and SARS-CoV-2 Antigen Expression in Sf9 Cells
content: The baculovirus expression vector system (BEVS) is widely used for recombinant protein production, yet culture medium choice critically affects cell growth and target yield. We evaluated the effects of six insect cell culture media on Sf9 cell proliferation, baculovirus replication, and SARS-CoV-2 N protein synthesis. Cells were adapted to three se-rum-supplemented (Grace's from Thermo Fisher Scientific, Himedia, and PanEco (PE)) and three serum-free (SFM from Tofflon Bio reagent (TBR), QuaCell (Qua), BioinnLabs (BIL)) media. Population doublings rate and viability were monitored. Cells were then in-fected with recombinant baculovirus carrying the N gene; viral titers and N protein expres-sion were subsequently assessed. SFM TBR and SFM Qua outperformed se-rum-supplemented media in supporting cell growth. However, SFM TBR failed to ensure efficient baculovirus replication or N protein accumulation despite robust cell prolifera-tion. In contrast, SFM Qua, especially with Feed A and Feed B supplements, enabled high viral titers and strong N protein expression. GIM PE and SFM BIL were unsuitable for Sf9 cultivation. We conclude that medium composition critically influences both proliferation and production. SFM Qua was identified as the most suitable for baculovirus-mediated SARS-CoV-2 N protein synthesis, emphasizing the need for medium optimization for each target product in BEVS.
